summary: Initial scoping for model selection and deployment mode for GraniteBay Retail. Customer needs multi-language product QA and shopping assistant with long context (product catalogs + conversation history), tool-calling to inventory/pricing APIs, and strict data residency/SOC2 requirements. Discussed open-model candidates, context length tradeoffs, hosted vs dedicated vs private options, and next steps to run benchmarks and share prompt set.
topics: deployment: hosted vs dedicated vs VPC/private
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-04-01
Time: 10:00 AM PDT
Duration: 48 minutes
Attendees: Samira Patel (Redwood AE), Diego Ramos (Redwood SE), Aisha Khan (GraniteBay - Head of ML), Tom Lowe (GraniteBay - Platform), Marta Ruiz (GraniteBay - Product)

--- Auto-generated summary (may be imperfect) ---
GraniteBay needs an LLM-backed shopping assistant and product QA flow that must operate across English, French, Spanish. Key constraints: long product catalogs + user convo history (want up to 65k tokens for sessions), tool-calling to internal inventory and pricing APIs, and enterprise controls (SOC2, SSO, VPC/KMS). Evaluating open models for cost/latency/accuracy.

Transcript:
[00:00] Samira (Redwood AE): Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick intros, we're Samira and Diego from Redwood. You wanna kick off Aisha?
[00:12] Aisha (GraniteBay): Yeah hi, thanks. I'm Aisha, Head of ML at GraniteBay. We're building a multilang shopping assistant and a product ingestion QA flow. Marta handles product, Tom's on infra.
[00:22] Tom (GraniteBay): Hi all.
[00:24] Marta (GraniteBay): Hey.
[00:26] Diego (Redwood SE): Great. Can you give us the high level on data and context length needs?
[00:32] Aisha: Sure. So our catalog per vertical is about ~1.2M SKUs, but the doc we pass to the model is mostly denormalized product info and recent user session history. Typical session we want the model to see is like product descriptions + 5–10 prior messages, and sometimes entire category extracts. We're seeing cases where a longer context helps, especially for cart reconstruction and price-check. Ideally we want 32k tokens as baseline, and some use cases up to 65k tokens.
[01:00] Samira: Got it. 32k baseline, 65k for certain flows. Are there particular latency SLOs? P95 or tail latency constraints?
[01:07] Aisha: We aim for sub-600ms p95 for chat quick-replies and up to 2s p95 for heavier QA that touches inventory. Throughput is variable — during campaigns we can spike to 2000 requests per minute.
[01:20] Diego: Helpful. For tool-calling — inventory and pricing APIs — are those synchronous internal services or long-running batch jobs?
[01:28] Tom: Mostly synchronous microservices, low-latency internal endpoints. We also have a pricing-on-demand job but that's separate.
[01:33] Marta: From product side, tool-calling is essential so the assistant returns live inventory and can trigger a hold on checkout.
[01:40] Samira: Understood. On deployment, do you have a preference? Hosted API to start? Dedicated capacity? Or private VPC?
[01:48] Aisha: Security is important — we're SOC2 in progress, and our legal requires customer data not leave EMEA for some customers. So ideally a VPC/private deployment in EU for regulated accounts. For pilot, maybe hosted EU region if isolation controls are strong. We want KMS integration and audit logs.
[02:05] Diego: Makes sense. We have three common pathways: Redwood Hosted (fastest), Redwood Dedicated (reserved GPU pools, predictable throughput), and Redwood Private (VPC/on-prem with KMS). Each has tradeoffs on cost and control. For the long context (65k) there are runtime considerations — memory/kv cache and model selection affect latency and cost.
[02:25] Aisha: Speaking of models — what open models are you recommending? We've seen Mistral, Llama 3, Mosaic-XL mentioned in other vendor notes. Also some teams refer to Falcon variants.
[02:35] Diego: Right. For open models we typically evaluate architecture vs sequence length and quality. Quick notes from our side: Mistral 7B and 7B-instruct are cost-effective for short contexts, Llama 3 13B gives better instruction following and multilingual performance, and Mosaic-XL or Llama 3 70B-class models are stronger for long-context and more complex reasoning. Falcon 40B can be good but tuning matters. Also there are quantized variants that reduce memory but sometimes degrade ranking quality.
[03:05] Marta: Are those all available via Redwood hosted catalog?
[03:09] Samira: Yes we host curated open models and have verified performance profiles. For Dedicated and Private, we can preload models into the customer's pool. For Private on-prem, you can bring-your-own-model too.
[03:18] Tom: For multilingual (EN/FR/ES) is Llama 3 recommended over Mistral? We've seen Mistral has weaker French in some benchmarks.
[03:26] Diego: Llama 3 and Mosaic-XL generally have stronger multilingual signal, especially with mid/large sizes. Mistral is improving but often needs more fine-tuning or instruction tuning on French/Spanish. Important: tokenization differences can affect token counts significantly across languages.
[03:42] Aisha: Good to know. Cost is a big driver. Can you ballpark cost differences between small models at 32k and large models at 65k?
[03:50] Samira: I'll share a cost spreadsheet, but rough rule: cost per token scales with model size and activation memory; a 13B optimized variant at 32k context can be 3-4x cheaper than a 70B at 65k context. Dedicated committed capacity reduces unit cost but requires commit.
[04:07] Diego: Also, runtime optimizations — continuous batching, prefix/KV cache, and quantization profiles — can cut cost. But for 65k context you often need models that support long-sequence kernels or you pay a lot in memory bandwidth.
[04:20] Marta: You mentioned KV cache — does Redwood manage cross-request caching of product embeddings or prefixes?
[04:26] Diego: Yes, we support prefix caching and KV cache reuse for repeated prefixes like product facts; it can dramatically reduce re-computation. We'll run an experiment to show gains for your workload.
[04:36] Tom: For VPC/private — what does the control plane look like? Is it fully customer-owned? How does KMS integrate?
[04:43] Samira: For Private deployments we provide a private control plane with customer-managed networking. You can integrate your KMS/HSM and we stream audit logs to your SIEM. For Dedicated we offer VPC peering and customer-managed subnets. We can map out the network flow in a follow-up diagram.
[04:58] Aisha: On data residency — can hosted EU region be sufficient for pilot?
[05:02] Samira: Yes, hosted EU region can be used; we can enable stricter retention windows and EU-only routing. But for regulatory customers, Private in-customer VPC is the recommended final approach.
[05:13] Diego: Back to model selection — can you share a small representative prompt set and some examples of tool calls so we can run throughput and accuracy tests?
[05:22] Aisha: We'll compile a set with English, French, Spanish prompts and sample API stubs. We want tests to include heavy catalog lookups and price recalculation tool calls.
[05:32] Marta: Also include edge cases — SKU merges, format inconsistencies.
[05:36] Diego: Good, that will let us test hallucination rates and instruction-following. We'll run evals across a few model candidates: Mistral 7B-instruct, Llama 3 13B, Mosaic-XL 8x/70B where available, and a Falcon 40B variant.
[05:52] Samira: For the pilot, we usually suggest starting with hosted or dedicated narrow pilot on EU region, evaluate latency and accuracy on your prompts, then decide if Private is required. Pilot steps: share prompt set, we run benchmarks + cost estimates, then you pick model and deployment.
[06:07] Tom: For throughput spikes — autoscaling on Dedicated vs Hosted — how does warmup affect tail latency when a new GPU instance spins up?
[06:15] Diego: We have burst capacity and can pre-warm instances based on rules. Warmup affects first-request latency for large models; for that reason, prefix caching and fast fallbacks to smaller models can help preserve latency SLOs.
[06:28] Aisha: Do you support tool-calling security — like signed tokens for inventory API and RBAC?
[06:34] Samira: Yes, tool-calls can be proxied through a Redwood gateway with short-lived tokens or you can integrate directly within your private network for Private deployments. RBAC and audit logs are available.
[06:44] Marta: Are there examples of similar retail customers?
[06:47] Samira: We have case studies in retail that used mixed model strategies — small models for quick answers, larger models for deep QA — plus tool-calling for inventory. I can share anonymized benchmark decks.
[06:56] Aisha: One technical question — sequence length support: do you have models that natively handle 65k, or do you stitch context via retrieval?
[07:04] Diego: Some models (larger Mosaic/Llama 70B variants and specialized long-context variants) have native 64k kernels. For others we recommend a retrieval+RAG approach where the model only receives condensed context plus a retrieval pass. It's a tradeoff between latency, accuracy, and cost. For product QA, retrieval with dense embeddings often works well and is cost-efficient.
[07:22] Marta: On embeddings — do you provide embedding indexes and vector stores or do we manage?
[07:27] Samira: Redwood integrates with common vector stores but you can also use our managed embedding indexing as an add-on. For Dedicated/Private customers you can self-host an index in your VPC.
[07:37] Tom: For compliance audits, what docs do you have? SOC2, ISO, penetration test reports?
[07:42] Samira: We have SOC2 Type II, ISO 27001 summary, and a security handbook. I'll attach the security pack. For Private we can sign stronger contracts and provide network diagrams.
[07:52] Aisha: Great. For the pilot I'd like to see two concrete experiments: (1) latency/quality comparison at 32k context across four models, (2) 65k end-to-end path for our heaviest flow to measure cost and tail latency.
[08:05] Diego: We'll set up those experiments. Quick note — 65k test will need either a long-context model or chunk+reconstruction logic; results will include cost per successful QA and the p50/p95 latencies.
[08:18] Samira: I'll send a proposed pilot plan after this call. Diego, can you take point on the benchmarking plan?
[08:24] Diego: Yep. I'll draft the plan and include the runtime config (batch sizes, quantization settings, kernel selection notes) and share it in the next 48 hours.
[08:33] Marta: About privacy — do you redact PII in logs or do you ship raw transcripts to Redwood for hosted?
[08:40] Samira: For hosted you can enable automatic redaction and shorter retention. For Private, logs stay in your environment and you control retention. We also support field-level redaction hooks.
[08:51] Tom: Any recommended batch size or config for 13B to balance latency and throughput?
[08:57] Diego: For 13B in a dedicated GPU (A100/80GB class) we usually start with batch sizes 4–8 for high concurrency, and 1–2 for low-latency interactive paths. We'll tune based on your QPS shape.
[09:12] Aisha: One more — do you support function-calling style tool invocation so the model returns structured calls?
[09:18] Diego: Yes, we support structured tool-calling and function-like responses; it's part of the runtime and we have examples for inventory/pricing. Implementation differs slightly across models, but we normalize outputs at the Redwood layer.
[09:31] Marta: Are there any gotchas with quantized weights and tool-calling? We saw hallucinations increase after heavy quantization in a lab run.
[09:40] Diego: Good question — aggressive 4-bit quantization sometimes changes probabilities leading to slightly different tokenization behavior; for tool-calling that requires strict JSON shapes we recommend mixed-precision or carefully validated quantized profiles. We'll include that in the benchmarking.
[09:56] Samira: OK wrapping up. Recap of next steps: Aisha to share prompt set and sample APIs by 4/8; Diego will run 32k and 65k experiments and share results and configs; Samira to send pricing and security pack; schedule pilot kickoff week of 4/18.
[10:18] Aisha: Sounds good. Thanks all.
[10:21] Samira: Thanks, we'll follow up with calendar invites and the spreadsheet. Bye.
[10:24] Call ends.

Notes on transcription: occasional mis-hearings - "KV cache" sometimes transcribed as "K V cash"; "Mosaic-XL" was heard as "mosaic ex ell" in parts. Numbers (32k/65k) sometimes become 32000/65000 in intermediate notes.
